Bug_Title: XSS: Servlet reflected cross site scripting vulnerability (XSS_REQUEST_PARAMETER_TO_SERVLET_WRITER)
Bug_Details:
This code directly writes an HTTP parameter to Servlet output, which allows for a reflected cross site scripting
vulnerability. See http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross-site_scripting
for more information. SpotBugs looks only for the most blatant, obvious cases of cross site scripting.
If SpotBugs found any, you almost certainly have more cross site scripting
vulnerabilities that SpotBugs doesn't report. If you are concerned about cross site scripting, you should seriously
consider using a commercial static analysis or pen-testing tool.
Bug_Explanation: This code directly writes an HTTP parameter to Servlet output, which allows for a reflected cross site scripting vulnerability. See http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross-site_scripting for more information.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case 'testShowBug' triggers the bug by passing a specially crafted string to the'showBug' method. This string contains a script tag that will cause an alert dialog to pop up when the response is displayed in a web browser, demonstrating the vulnerability.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: Based on the provided test results, the bug is confirmed to be triggered. The test execution results show that the input 'name=<script>alert('XSS')</script>' is reflected in the output as it is. This is a clear indication of the bug being present in the Java code.
